its examples page says its main tutorial shows use “in a web browser.” The same official examples page says there are separate `examples/node/` examples for Node.js usage.

evidence_passages.text: The current official Node text-extraction example does **not** import the generic build; it imports `pdfjs-dist/legacy/build/pdf.mjs`.

claims.text: That Node example extracts page text by calling `await pdfPage.getTextContent()` and joining `item.str` values from `items`.

evidence_passages.text: That example loads a document with `getDocument({ url: pdfPath })`, gets each page with `getPage(i)`, calls `await pdfPage.getTextContent()`, and prints `items.map(item => item.str).join(" ")`.

claims.text: The API docs say `PDFPageProxy.getTextContent()` returns a promise for `TextContent`; whitespace is normalized to standard spaces, and `TextContent` includes `items` and `styles` with `TextItem.str` as the text string.

evidence_passages.text: The public API docs say `PDFPageProxy.getTextContent()` returns a promise for a `TextContent` object, and that all whitespace is normalized to standard spaces (`0x20`).
The `TextContent` docs say it contains an `items` array plus `styles`; `TextItem.str` is the text string

claims.text: Current PDF.js source explicitly warns Node.js users to use the legacy build, and the FAQ lists `Node.js 22+` only under the `legacy` build as mostly supported with limited automated testing; Bun is not listed there.
acceptable_patterns: Please use the legacy build in Node\.js environments

evidence_passages.text: For Node-like environments, the current source explicitly warns: `Please use the legacy build in Node.js environments.`

The current FAQ says PDF.js ships a default non-polyfilled build for the latest browsers and a separate `legacy` build for older environments; in its support table, `Node.js 22+` appears under the `legacy` build as “Mostly” supported with “Limited” automated testing. Bun is not listed in that table.

claims.text: The documented runtime assumptions relevant to Bun compatibility include Node-specific APIs and environment-sensitive defaults: PDF.js uses `process.getBuiltinModule(...)`, `createRequire(...)`, `fs/promises.readFile`, may load `@napi-rs/canvas` to polyfill `DOMMatrix` and `Path2D`, and in Node.js defaults `useWorkerFetch`, `isOffscreenCanvasSupported`, and `isImageDecoderSupported` to `false` while defaulting `disableFontFace` to `true`.

evidence_passages.text: The runtime defaults in `src/display/api.js` are environment-sensitive. In Node.js, `useWorkerFetch` defaults to `false`, `isOffscreenCanvasSupported` defaults to `false`, `isImageDecoderSupported` defaults to `false`, `disableFontFace` defaults to `true`

`node_utils.js` shows what those Node defaults assume at runtime: it uses `process.getBuiltinModule("module").createRequire(...)`, tries to load `@napi-rs/canvas`, polyfills `DOMMatrix` and `Path2D` from that package when possible, synthesizes a minimal `navigator` if `navigator.language` is missing, and reads local files through `fs/promises.readFile`.
